headline: Count prefix differences while merging sorted halves
statement: Count nonempty contiguous subarrays whose sum lies in the inclusive interval [lower, upper].
intuition: A subarray sum is prefix[j]-prefix[i] for i<j. Divide prefix positions into original-order halves. All cross-half pairs have valid index order; after sorting each half by value, two monotone right-half boundaries count differences inside the interval.
approach: Create prefix sums including the initial zero.
Recursively count pairs inside each half.
For each sorted left value, move two right pointers to the first difference >= lower and first difference > upper.
Add their distance, then merge the two halves into sorted order.
correctness: Every index pair belongs uniquely to a recursive left half, right half, or cross-half pair. Recursive calls count the first two classes. For cross pairs, sorted right values make the accepted differences a contiguous interval, counted exactly by the two boundaries. Sorting only after partitioning preserves the original index-order relation at every level.
bruteForce: Accumulate each start/end subarray sum, taking O(n²). Merge-sort counting reduces work by processing whole monotone value ranges.

complexity.explanation: Each recursion level does linear counting and merging using a reusable buffer.

pitfalls: Include the zero prefix to count subarrays starting at index zero.
Use <= upper but < lower for the two boundaries.
Sorting all prefix sums before dividing would lose index order.
